name: Saint Rose of Lima
history: Isabel Flores de Oliva, called Rose for her beauty as a baby, lived a hidden life of prayer and penance in her family’s garden in Lima, while caring for the sick and poor of the city. A Dominican tertiary, she died at thirty-one and was the first canonised saint of the Americas.
life: Rose was born in Lima, then the capital of Spain’s South American empire. Taking Saint Catherine of Siena as her model, she refused offers of marriage and in 1606 became a lay member of the Dominican order. She lived in a tiny hermitage in her parents’ garden and supported her struggling family by fine needlework and by growing flowers to sell. She took into her home sick and destitute people, among them Indians and African slaves, and nursed them herself. Her penances were severe, and her confessors and friends sometimes urged her to moderation. She also endured long years of spiritual darkness. Many in Lima, rich and poor, came to her for prayer and counsel, and when she died in 1617 the whole city mourned. Clement X canonised her in 1671. She is patron of Peru, of Latin America and of the Philippines.
prayerTo: Saint Rose, you loved Christ in hiddenness and served Him in the poor of your city. Pray for the peoples of Latin America and for all who are poor and sick. Help me to find God in ordinary work, and to give Him my heart without holding anything back. Amen.
penance: Do some quiet, ordinary work today with care, as Rose did her needlework and gardening, and offer what you earn or save to help the sick.
meditation: Rose is remembered to have said that apart from the cross there is no other ladder by which we may get to heaven. What cross is in front of you today, and will you climb it or walk around it?
